raw_response:
I'll think through this year's plan like I do every spring — starting from what I did last year and what worked.

My 10.1 mu is all wheat-maize rotation, same as everyone around here in Quzhou. I don't have land to waste trying new systems.

**Wheat (winter):** I plant in early October after maize comes off. I buy improved seed from the agricultural supply shop in town — Jimai or Shimai varieties, whatever the dealer has fresh. Seed rate around 15 kg per mu because our autumn has been dry lately, I push it a little higher to get a good stand.

For fertilizer, I use compound fertilizer (15-15-15 or similar) as base, about 50 kg per mu before plowing, then topdress with urea at jointing stage, about 20-25 kg urea per mu. That gives me roughly 22 kg N, 8 kg P, 8 kg K per mu total. I'd rather put a bit extra than come up short — losing 50 kg of grain hurts more than spending an extra 30 yuan on fertilizer. I have well irrigation so I water 3 times: after sowing if dry, at jointing, and at grain filling. Spray herbicide once in spring, and fungicide plus aphid spray at heading — that's 2 applications, sometimes 3 if aphids are bad. Rotary tillage after maize, no time to plow deep between seasons. I expect around 500 kg per mu if weather is normal.

**Maize (summer):** Straight after wheat in mid-June. I always buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or Denghai type, whatever the neighbors had good results with. No-till direct seeding into wheat stubble, that's what most of us do now. Base fertilizer I put down with the planter, compound fertilizer around 40 kg per mu. Then I topdress urea at the big trumpet stage, about 25 kg per mu. Total around 20 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Irrigate once or twice depending on summer rains — usually once at tasseling is enough. Spray for corn borer and armyworm, 2 applications. Expect 550 kg per mu.

I'm watching my money — fertilizer and seed for both crops runs me nearly 500 yuan per mu. But I don't cut fertilizer to save money. My father always said hungry soil gives hungry harvest.
